claims.statement: AddBotFarm allows anonymous access to Account Razor Pages, authorizes the rest of the Razor Pages folder, and uses the Identity application cookie in Production or the synthetic Development authentication scheme as the default scheme.

Login redirects to setup when no Identity user exists; setup verifies the setup code before validating required fields and password confirmation, creates the account only while the user store is empty, and signs the created user in.

The TestBot dashboard renders the shared BotDashboard layout, which composes backup, chat, webhook, and stats cards for the given bot name, and the shared layout builds a navigation link for each registered bot module.

DashboardChats resolves the bot's database and bot services from IBotRegistry by name, loads known chat IDs up front, fetches Telegram chat details only for uncached chats on the current table page with at most five concurrent requests, caches fetched names until Refresh, and shows a failed lookup as an uncached unavailable row while the page continues loading.

DashboardBackups supports listing, creating, downloading, deleting, and restoring archives; delete and restore require confirmation. Creation ignores overlapping requests and changes the create control's label while running, while delete and restore controls are disabled during active operations.

The host dashboard displays memory and uptime, lists log files from the data folder for viewing or download, and its confirmed shutdown action stops the host without pausing bot webhooks; the authenticated shutdown API can pause all bots first through PauseAllForShutdownAsync.

The /health endpoint requires the HealthReader policy, which accepts an authenticated user from the admin scheme (Identity cookie or development scheme) or the HealthApiKey scheme fed by HealthChecks:ApiKey; admin pages use only the default admin scheme, so the key opens nothing else.

Focused account tests cover first-run and existing-user redirects, checking the setup code first, invalidating it after use, concurrent setup, successful setup and sign-in, invalid credentials, and login lockout.

The shared BotEnabledControl, used by the host dashboard and the bot webhook card, submits an explicit enabled target or retry request, disables the switch while working or for unknown, pending, error or unconfirmed states, and presents pending, unknown, or error feedback with retry where applicable.

Bot on/off actions ignore repeat clicks while in flight; a coordinator busy response displays an informational notice, while other failures are logged by exception type without provider exception text being shown in the control's error message.

SetupCodeService holds the first-run setup code in memory, taking it from Setup:Code (rejecting values shorter than 16 characters without revealing them) or generating a random 16-byte base64url code, verifies it in constant time, and erases it after creating the first user inside a lock that re-checks that no user exists.

SetupAnnouncementHostedService logs the generated setup code, or a reminder naming the setting for a configured code, when no admin exists, and logs a warning without the code if the identity store is unreachable.

The dark-mode preference is stored in a darkModePreference cookie that App.razor reads server-side for the first render; without it, MainLayout reads the browser's system preference after first render and persists it.
The Chats table offers per-cell copy buttons for chat name and ID that are hidden until hover on hover-capable devices and disables sending for unavailable chats.
Signing out requires an antiforgery-validated POST to the Logout page, which the layout's sign-out form sends with an antiforgery token; a GET only redirects home.

SendMessageDialog loads a per-dialog JS module that creates a Quill editor limited to Telegram HTML formats including a tg-spoiler spoiler, converts its content to Telegram-compatible HTML, and sends it through INotificationService or hands it to an optional submit handler, keeping the dialog open on empty content, failure, or a declining handler and ignoring overlapping sends.
MainLayout defines a custom MudTheme with light and dark palettes, a violet primary accent, Inter typography, and 10px default border radius.

The Chats table cuts chat names longer than 45 user-perceived characters with an ellipsis via FormatUtils.Truncate, shows the full name in a tooltip only for shortened names, and copies the full name.
Chat clean-up checks every known chat with Telegram at most five at a time, and after confirmation deletes only chats classified as unreachable, keeping chats whose check failed for other reasons.

Send to all opens the message editor with a confirming submit handler, then broadcasts through IBroadcastService with progress and reports unreachable and failed counts, finishing even when the page is closed.

The webhook card shows Telegram's webhook URL, pending update count and last error, and enables dropping pending updates only when updates are queued and the bot is not pending, reloading the info afterwards.

The log viewer shows a loading state marked aria-busy until the file is read, filters entries by level, renders at most the newest 5,000 matching entries, and polls live .log files every three seconds for appended entries.
BotDashboard lets a bot replace the standard stats card through its Stats parameter and append cards via MainExtra, SideExtra and ChildContent.

The /dashboard/health page is an authorized component that runs every registered health check through HealthCheckService on load and on Refresh, lists each check sorted by name with status, description, duration, data and exception, and reports a failed run as an error notification.
The shared layout's drawer links Health to /dashboard/health.

Admin-existence checks in login, setup, setup completion and the startup announcement use HasAnyUserAsync, which awaits MongoDB's AnyAsync for a MongoDB user store and falls back to a synchronous Any otherwise.

The host dashboard's uptime ticks in the browser via js/uptime.js, started once from the server uptime after first render, and the page disposes the ticker when left, including while the module or ticker is still starting.

The home page mounts an SVG night-city scene from js/city.js that drives each bot module as an emoji car linking to its dashboard, shows a live uptime panel, honors prefers-reduced-motion with static cars, and is disposed when the page is left.
